title: Grateful Dead Live at The Omni on 1990-04-02
lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
source: 2 Nakamichi CM300s/ CP4's  w/1 Nakamichi CM300/CP2>  Nakamichi 550 w/Maxell XLIIS90 cassette masters. Dolby B was used on the Master Cassettes. OTS 8 foot stand (sec. 128 Row CC Seat11)

ai_review.summary: Nice audience recording captures a strong ending to Looks Like Rain and an especially good Death Don't performance.
ai_review.review: The audience tape is clear enough for a pleasant listening experience, and the show features a powerful finish to "Looks Like Rain" plus a standout rendition of "Death Don't Hurt Me." Reviewers note an interesting vocal cadence from Bob Weir and Brent Mydland on "He's Gone," though it ends abruptly into "Last Time," and Jerry Garcia’s phrasing on the final verse shows him pulling back before the band joins in.

ai_rating.rationale: Only one detailed review; it rates the show 4 stars, praising key moments and noting a decent audience recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewer calls it a "nice aud recording" with no complaints about clarity or drop‑outs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Interesting setlist with a strong closing to Looks Like Rain; the transition from He's Gone into Last Time feels abrupt.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Sounds like Jerry was pulling back on the last verse of Death Don't before the band came in.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob and Brent’s vocal cadence on He's Gone is highlighted as interesting but ends too quickly.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s vocal contribution noted alongside Bob on He's Gone.
